epic.title: compat(window): BaseWindow/BrowserWindow over the host window registry — identity, cancelable close, ready-to-show, chrome options
epic.body:
## Scope
32 entities / 606 raw members: `BaseWindow` (187) and `BrowserWindow` (204, 126 inherited), constructor option structures (52 + 2 fields), `WebPreferences` (46 fields), `View`/`WebContentsView`/`BrowserView`/`ImageView`, 11 TouchBar classes (macOS), JumpList/Thumbar structures (Windows). Live today: the host owns exactly one primary window per session, created after the authenticated HELLO before Bun code runs; close is uncancelable; no window id crosses kipc; no chrome options exist; the destination window registry is TARGET.

## Corpus demand
Constructor + `show:false` + `ready-to-show` + `backgroundColor` (Zettlr 14 sites, draw.io), cancelable `close` with async veto then explicit `destroy()` (both apps), `closed` bookkeeping, `isDestroyed`, `getAllWindows/getFocusedWindow/fromWebContents`, maximize/minimize/fullscreen state + events, macOS `hiddenInset` + `trafficLightPosition`, Windows/Linux `frame:false` + `titleBarOverlay` (Zettlr), parent/modal (Zettlr), `setWindowOpenHandler` with `overrideBrowserWindowOptions` (draw.io).

## Maturity ladder
- L0: `BrowserWindow` class exists; unsupported options throw typed errors (privilege-escalating `webPreferences` fail loudly; engine-only flags are ignored with a diagnostic).
- L1: electron-quick-start runs unmodified on macOS (`new BrowserWindow`, `loadFile`, `getAllWindows`, close → closed).
- L2: two-phase close, tombstone-before-`closed`, `show:false`/`ready-to-show`, state events pass conformance entries citing the pinned `browser-window.md`/`base-window.md` sentences; the window-state mirror is proven coherent under a 10k-event stream.
- L3: draw.io and Zettlr window workflows pass under `keld dev` with KEL-74 records.

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-139/KEL-142 (host-created primary window, bridge), KEL-143 (window survives Bun generation loss), KEL-75 (WindowGeneration minting, window-bound roles), KEL-135 (profiles), KEL-132 (GPU/media), KEL-98 (contract codegen is NOT general — a window channel needs its own contract owner), KEL-64 (double-rAF technique for paint oracle).

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters)
- The host mints opaque `(WindowId, WindowGeneration)`; the facade keeps a synchronous mirror updated by ordered host events before any user listener runs. `getAllWindows()` ordering is Keld-stronger than Electron (documented ▲-stronger).
- The host already creates the primary window before Bun runs; the first `new BrowserWindow()` adopts it (explicitly recorded) until Ready is re-based (F01-T2).
- Two-phase close owned by the host: `CloseRequested{window, generation, seq}` → facade emits `close` synchronously → `CloseAllow`/veto reply. The host waits indefinitely while the owning Bun generation is alive (Electron's delegate returns NO and waits); it closes on its own only when the generation is revoked. No host auto-close on timeout.
- Tombstone flips before `closed`; later member access throws the exact `Object has been destroyed` text; `destroy()` skips `close` and guarantees `closed`.
- `WebPreferences` triage: privilege-escalating fields (nodeIntegration, contextIsolation:false, webSecurity:false, allowRunningInsecureContent, enableBlinkFeatures, experimentalFeatures) fail loudly ✘; engine-flag fields such as `disableBlinkFeatures` (draw.io sets it on every window) are ignored with a diagnostic ▲; `sandbox:false` is ▲ ignored-with-diagnostic and never selects a Keld profile.
- One `BaseWindow` implementation; `BrowserWindow = BaseWindow + exactly one host-created content view`; View tree, BrowserView and multi-view are Tier 3.

## Platform lanes
macOS first (titleBarStyle/trafficLightPosition via public NSWindow API; vibrancy is Tier 2 ▲), Windows (frame:false + titleBarOverlay needs the WebView2 non-client receipt — open research F02-A6), Linux (GTK CSD).

decision_tickets.title: Can `show:false` + `ready-to-show` + `backgroundColor` be honoured on system webviews (hidden-paint oracle)?
decision_tickets.question: Electron fires `ready-to-show` when the renderer first renders while hidden. Keld must create the native window unmapped and derive ready-to-show from a host-owned isolated-world double-rAF reporter per engine (the KEL-64 technique, not its benchmark instrument). WebView2 stops rendering when the controller is invisible (receipt needed). Cheapest experiment: in the existing hello, create the window without ordering it front on each OS and observe whether the first paint beacon fires while hidden; record per-engine ✔/▲.

No mechanism is named that lets a red entry coexist with a green required gate.

invariant_violations.violation: Unattributed performance acceptance: 'zero steady-state allocation per read' and '10k-event/s' are asserted as ACs with no metric id, census, clock or allocation oracle (AGENTS: performance decompositions must separate census/work/queue/clock/statistic/artifact). The 'no steady-state allocation' rule applies to hot kipc/event-loop/guard paths in Rust; a JS facade getter has no observable for it.

ambiguity_laundering.claim: MAP lists 'Close and quit vetoes are async AppKit hooks; deadline expiry keeps the window open' under Decisions so far (resolved) while PANEL-D19 'CONTESTED: close-veto deadline expiry semantics' is open and gates F02-T2.
ambiguity_laundering.problem: The same atom is simultaneously resolved and contested. D19's own text says the judges settled the outcome and only the unhealthy-role signal remains open.
ambiguity_laundering.fix: D5: RESOLVED — on no reply the window stays open; host closes only on generation revocation. D19 retitled 'UNKNOWN: unhealthy-role diagnostic shape and threshold when a close-veto reply never arrives'.

ambiguity_laundering.claim: 'The host waits indefinitely while the owning Bun generation is alive (Electron's delegate returns NO and waits).'
ambiguity_laundering.problem: The receipt in PANEL-D5 supports only 'windowShouldClose: notifies and returns NO'. Electron does not wait on anything — the 'close' emit is synchronous on the browser UI thread and the window simply stays open (the F02 semantics refuter refuted the earlier deadline clause on exactly this point). 'and waits' is an inference about a pending state Electron does not have.
ambiguity_laundering.fix: FACT (v44.4.5 electron_ns_window_delegate.mm, as receipted in PANEL-D5): windowShouldClose: calls NotifyWindowCloseButtonClicked and returns NO; the close decision is made synchronously in the main process. INFERENCE: Keld's asynchronous equivalent is to keep the window open with no host timer.

ambiguity_laundering.claim: 'draw.io close dance (preventDefault every close → renderer isModified → decision → destroy) completes'.
ambiguity_laundering.problem: The 'decision' step is dialog.showMessageBoxSync (:876), which the plan elsewhere scaffolds as a typed throw; whether it can work at all is the open PANEL-P1 kill condition. The AC reads as an achievable fact.

verdicts.correction: The dead-Bun deadline rule collides with KEL-143's goal (same native window survives Bun generation loss): if the host honors a user close while no Bun generation is live, the window count can reach zero and LastWindowClosed has no listener generation. State the rule as its own atom: a close during generation loss either (a) is honored and the next generation receives a synthetic LastWindowClosed on admission, or (b) is parked until the admission deadline. Pick one in the registry spec; do not leave it as 'medium confidence'. Engine beforeunload support remains [unknown] on all three engines; no repo evidence exists.

verdicts.reason: The two-phase protocol shape (host CloseRequested -> facade 'close' with preventDefault -> CloseAllow -> unload -> destroy webview before window -> Closed; destroy() skips close but guarantees closed; destroyed-object fence) is confirmed by docs and source. But the deadline clause is justified by a false Electron fact: 'Electron's observable user can always close wins over a dead veto'. In Electron the 'close' emit is synchronous on the browser-process UI thread (electron_ns_window_delegate.mm:411-414 `windowShouldClose` calls NotifyWindowCloseButtonClicked and returns NO; native_window.cc:548-555 observers_.Notify(WillCloseWindow,&prevent_default); electron_api_base_window.cc:165-169 `if (Emit("close")) *prevent_default = true`). A blocked or slow main process therefore keeps the window OPEN in Electron; the user cannot 'always close'. As written, a slow-but-alive Bun (drawio's close handler ALWAYS preventDefaults then awaits an async renderer round-trip, electron.js:947-966, with destroy() only after 'saveAndClose-result'/'draftRemoved', :893-945) would have the host close the window on deadline and lose unsaved work — the exact failure the protocol exists to prevent.

verdicts.correction: Keep the protocol; replace the deadline clause with: the host waits for CloseAllow/CloseVeto indefinitely while the owning Bun generation is alive (matches Electron's observable: a non-answering main keeps the window open), and releases the pending close ONLY on supervisor-confirmed generation death (KEL-143 seam), recorded as a Keld ▲ policy, not Electron parity. Add: a CloseRequested that arrives while a previous one is still unanswered for the same WindowGeneration must coalesce (Electron re-emits 'close' per attempt; drawio keys each attempt with a fresh uniqueIsModifiedId, so re-emission per native attempt is the parity behaviour — but CloseAllow must carry the seq it answers). Keep DOM-beforeunload engine support as the stated unknown.

FACT: CloseAllWindows snapshots the window list, reverses it on macOS, and calls Close() on every window without re-checking the quitting flag (shell/browser/window_list.cc at v44.4.5).
FACT: a close-event preventDefault calls WindowList::WindowCloseCancelled, and Browser::OnWindowCloseCancelled then sets is_quitting_ to false (native_window.cc and browser.cc at v44.4.5).

decisions.question: How are close/closed/destroy/'Object has been destroyed' reproduced when the host owns the window and app code runs in a separate Bun process?
decisions.proposed_answer: [inference, evidence-backed] Two-phase close owned by the host: (1) native close request (button, Cmd+W, app.quit sweep, parent close) -> host emits CloseRequested{window, generation, seq} and does NOT close; (2) facade emits 'close' synchronously to listeners; if no listener called preventDefault, facade replies CloseAllow(seq); host then runs page unload, destroys the webview before the window (view_drop_order invariant), decrements the lifecycle window count, and emits Closed; (3) `win.destroy()` is a separate unconditional Destroy call that skips 'close' but guarantees 'closed' (Electron contract); (4) after Closed the facade fences the handle: every method/property except isDestroyed() throws Error('Object has been destroyed'). Deadline: if the Bun generation is dead or does not answer within the admission deadline, the host honors the user's close (window closes) — Electron's observable 'user can always close' wins over a dead veto; this is an explicit ▲ to record. 'close' must precede DOM beforeunload (Electron order), so the host must not start unload before CloseAllow.
